title: Context tricks & small-cache readings — quick log
content:
Purpose: quick scratchpad for several short reads I did this week on context handling strategies (prefix caching, chunking, and lightweight distillation). Want an agenda for a short brownbag and a follow-up experiment plan (microbench + quality probes).

Quick takeaways (TL;DR):
- Prefix/KV caching still gives the biggest wins for conversational apps when you can reuse context. But eviction policy matters a lot in long-lived sessions: LRU isn't enough for semantically important spans.
- Chunking / windowed attention + overlapping stitching is very promising for streaming long inputs — lower memory but fragile for exactness across boundaries.
- Quantization (4-bit + GPTQ-like) is attractive for cost, but interactive latency and KV cache representational fidelity can regress if quantization is aggressive; test with small probes.
- Retrieval + short context caching beats keeping huge contexts in RAM for many product workloads (cheap and more robust).

Papers/blogs I skimmed (notes):
1) "Sparse Key-Value Caches for LLMs" (arXiv 2023) — link above.
   - Idea: compress and sparsify saved KV entries, allow approximate retrieval.
   - Notes: their eval uses synthetically repeated prefixes; need to test on real dialog logs (CS triage, product chat).
   - Open question: how hard to integrate with our runtime without changing attention kernels? Seems feasible if we implement a thin lookup layer before KV assembly.

2) "Boundary Stitching: Windowed Attention for Long Inputs" (fast blog draft)
   - Author's claim: overlapping windows with cross-window alignment reduces hallucinations at stitch points.
   - Implementation notes: requires deterministic tokenization and checksum to detect seam drift. Could run as a lightweight post-filter in the stream aggregator.
   - Concern: extra latency for alignment step; maybe run alignment async and fallback to best-local chunk.

3) "GPTQ-like quantization & KV cache fidelity" (community thread + repo)
   - Tests I ran locally on a tiny checkpoint: 4-bit quantized model gives ~1.6x throughput, but token-level logit variance causes some early-stop tokens to change in short prompts.
   - For cached KV reuse: need to validate that quantized and non-quantized cache entries are compatible; mixing causes mismatch. Plan: canonicalize cache storage format and annotate quantization profile in metadata.

Ideas for small experiments (2–3 day sprints):
- Exp A (replay quality): pick 500 real user sessions (anonymized) and replay baseline (no cache), full prefix cache, and sparse-kv variant. Measure latency, tokens-per-second, and reply-quality using automatic metrics (ROUGE for repeats, perplexity delta) + small human check set (10 sessions).
- Exp B (stitching demo): implement minimal windowed-attention wrapper in python runtime shim: chunk input into 2k tokens windows with 256 token overlap, stitch by biasing beam scores at seams. Run on long-doc summarization pipeline. Check alignment errors.
- Exp C (quant mix tests): create KV store with metadata flags for quant profile. Run cross-compatibility tests: fill cache with fp16 entries then load under 4-bit model and compare outputs.

Notes-to-self / reminders:
- Ask runtime folks (Mika) whether we can add a small hook to the KV loader to return both raw tensors + quant_profile string. If yes, we can avoid cache corruption silently.
- Put a tiny dashboard for seam errors (mismatched tokens at window boundaries) — simple counters to start.
- Draft talk for brownbag: 20-minute sync; slides: problem framing, 2 mini-demos (cache replay + stitch demo), open questions.

Unresolved questions (brain dump):
- How to define "important span" for eviction? Could use attention-salience or retrieval frequency rather than time-based LRU. Needs lightweight compute.
- Is there a cheap indexable fingerprint for semantic spans that is small enough to store alongside KV entries? (minhash / simhash?)
- Can we exploit model internals (attention head activations) to detect reusable context cheaply? Might be invasive.

Next actions (week of 2026-06-22):
- Sync with Mika for KV loader metadata hook (blocker for quant mix tests).
- Prepare minimal dataset: 500 anonymized sessions + 10 hand-checked sessions. Coordinate with privacy.
- Prototype stitching shim and measure seam error rate on 50 docs.

Random links / bookmarks saved:
- arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.17580
- Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache-protos (local PR referenced above)
- Slack thread: #kv-cache-discuss/thread-8672 (notes from Evan)

Short summary I can paste into brownbag invite: "Rapid notes from this week's reading: KV caching + clever eviction and windowed stitching seem like the most operationally useful levers to reduce cost and keep latency low for long-context apps. I'd like to propose three small experiments (replay, stitch demo, quant-compat) to validate on real session traces and bring back concrete recommendations for production defaults."

Personal quick rating (how excited I am): 7/10 — interesting tradeoffs between simplicity and fidelity, so we can get practical wins fast if we keep experiments small and measurable.

End of scratchpad.

(Notes: this document is a working draft; will prune before sharing outside eng-applied-ml.)
